sources.license: PMC author manuscript; article text is not redistributed. Curated factual summaries only.
sources.coverage: Selected RNA processing, annotation and atlas coverage paragraphs; supplementary marker table S2 has not been imported.

sources.title: Single-cell transcriptome atlases of soybean root and mature nodule reveal new regulatory programs that control the nodulation process
sources.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; factual associations and original summaries only, article text not redistributed.
sources.coverage: Methods p0220, p0230 and p0235 plus the previously curated 62 explicit marker associations. Not the complete supplementary marker tables.

sources.title: Cross-species plant single-cell analysis: community challenges and shared solutions
sources.citation: Haghani et al., Journal of Experimental Botany (2026)
sources.license: Crossref publisher-deposited abstract metadata; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 listed for accepted manuscript. Only factual summary redistributed.
sources.coverage: Publisher-deposited abstract only. The full guide and its tables have not been ingested.

passages.title: RNA and chromatin assays cover different nuclei
passages.summary: The atlas reports RNA profiles from seven tissues and chromatin profiles from ten. Root is included. RNA and ATAC are separate measurements; accessibility is not measured transcript abundance.
passages.locator: Results, atlas generation; paragraph P10
passages.applicability: Study context, not evidence that any particular cluster has a specific identity.

passages.title: Published RNA processing and genome build
passages.summary: RNA reads were mapped to Williams 82 v4. The workflow removes low-quality nuclei and doublets, normalizes with SCTransform, integrates replicates with Harmony, then computes UMAP and clusters in Seurat. These are published processing steps, not operations newly performed by Celloras.
passages.locator: STAR Methods, snRNA-seq data processing; paragraph P64
passages.applicability: Check the imported assay and layer before calculating expression; this paragraph does not prove what any exported matrix layer contains.

passages.title: How the atlas assigned biological labels
passages.summary: Atlas labels combine published markers, ortholog relationships and gene-set enrichment. Ambiguous clusters with similar marker patterns may share a broader label.
passages.locator: STAR Methods, cell type annotation; paragraph P69 and cited Table S2
passages.applicability: Cluster numbers are dataset-specific group identifiers, not transferable biological names. This collection has not imported the cited v4 marker table; review it before transferring labels.

passages.title: A different reference build from the multiomic atlas
passages.summary: This study aligned RNA reads to Glycine_max_v2.1.52, then processed background contamination, doublets, normalization, integration and clustering.
passages.locator: Methods, processing sNucRNA-seq datasets; paragraph p0220
passages.applicability: Celloras requires a verified mapping before transferring gene associations to the v4 atlas, even when Glyma identifiers look alike. A build mismatch is not evidence against a biological identity.

passages.title: Spatial validation and orthology have different evidence strength
passages.summary: The study localized selected root markers using Molecular Cartography. Some identities outside the sampled cross-section were inferred using marker orthology. Evidence obtained in soybean tissue and evidence transferred from related species should remain distinguishable.
passages.locator: Results, soybean root atlas annotation; paragraph p0030
passages.applicability: Study-level validation context. It does not experimentally validate an annotation of the user's cells.

passages.title: A roadmap for tools coordinated with literature
passages.summary: The community roadmap calls for evolutionary context in annotation and agents that coordinate analysis tools with literature. It describes priorities and proposed approaches, not a benchmark validating Celloras predictions.
passages.locator: Abstract, publisher-deposited Crossref record
passages.applicability: General plant research context; no soybean gene association or cell identity is established by this passage.
